shared_elements: low-relief carving on a rough, pale stone pillar face
bird-like creature in profile with a prominent hooked beak
long sinuous curved line reading as a snake or serpentine body
outdoor excavated setting with rubble stonework beside the carved block
justification: Both are flat-faced stone pillars bearing shallow relief in the same pale, granular stone, and each carries a profile bird with a hooked beak plus a long sinuous serpentine line and an angular zigzag element, which is a fairly specific overlap of motifs. The decisive difference is density and organisation: A holds one or two faint, isolated, very lightly incised figures on an otherwise blank field, whereas B is a crowded, register-based composition with a horizontal patterned band, rows of discs and animals, and far bolder, deeper modelling.
